areas.name: Ocala National Forest
areas.description:
-Does require a permit to ride here, follow link.

Ocala forest is one of the largest areas you can ride in Central Florida area.  Both plated and
OHV can ride here, though in their respective areas. Most start from the south area (Wandering Wiregrass) or the north area (Rodman Dam trailhead).  Can find many GPX files in the Facebook files tabes.

areas.name: Richloam WMA
areas.description:
Richloam is special.  Its mainly a wildlife management area for hunting and camping, but because of that there are trails everywhere.  It's known for its swampy type water holes and black mud.  Expect to get wet during the rainy seasons.  But also probably some of the best trail riding you can do 
in FL.

Most meet at the FireTower\Ranger station as there is plenty of parking and a good central starting point.  Just across the street is the Richloam General Store.

areas.name: Croom Motorcycle Area
areas.description:
Off-highway vehicle enthusiasts in Central Florida will find miles of trails within the 2,600-acre Croom Motorcycle Area (CMA) at Withlacoochee State Forest.

Croom is used by all types of riders, from pro motorcross racers to weekend riders.  Expect to see lots of people riding, including ATVs.  There is even a technical riding area you can sign up to us.

Onsite campground with RV hookups.

areas.name: Citrus WMA
areas.description:
Only street-legal, plated dual-sport motorcycles are permitted to ride within the Citrus Wildlife Management Area (WMA). While the sprawling 50,000-acre terrain features highly dynamic elevation changes and technical challenges,

• The Sugar Sand Challenge: For heavy dual-sports or street-biased adventure tires, the thick sugar sand sections (especially on central tracks like Trail 11 and Trail 15) can be a real hurdle. Maintaining momentum and bringing proper off-road tire pressure is key.
• Trail 19 (The Technical Test): If you want a challenge, Trail 19 is a notorious 1-mile stretch featuring massive ruts, steep washouts, and switchbacks up to 4 feet deep. It is widely considered one of the most technically challenging public tracks in Florida.
• Trail 14 (The Big Dip): This route features deep depressions and steep terrain changes that test your front-end clearance and climbing traction.
